changes: Registered native release verification on x86_64 admits every proof backing capacity and a combined cumulative request bound before creating configuration, copying public values or performing numerical verification.
Fresh reference configuration obtains two independent CSPRNG seeds directly from OS entropy, avoiding thread-local RNG storage and reporting entropy failure explicitly.

The configuration derivation counts five Poseidon2 constant sets, empty Arc-backed DFT caches and GPU-feature MMCS/RNG wrapper allocations. Public copying requests exact capacity and diagnostic formatting uses a fixed 1024-byte UTF-8 buffer before one final String allocation.
A read-only accessor in pinned p3-symmetric 0.6.1 exposes hidden Merkle-cap spare capacity. No hashes, encodings, proof fields or arithmetic change.

Standard, wide and non-stream CPU tests and research tests check capacity mutations and allocator conformance; two full-size finalizers preserve registry identity and all sixteen proving arithmetic stages on OpenCL.
limitations: The temporary component bounds cumulative Rust allocation requests, including replacements, for the native registered single-machine entry point. Caller proof backing capacity has its own 64 MiB ceiling, checked after allocation has already occurred; the borrowed check cannot reserve the caller retroactively.

A borrowed public slice does not expose its owner capacity. Cached verifier metadata, caller/result retention, callbacks, stacks, allocator and OS/libc entropy-provider overhead require enclosing lifetime admission.

The source-derived model is qualified for release x86_64 on this Linux host using the pinned p3 dependencies and Rust 1.96. Other verifier families, debug symbolic inference and other targets remain outside the model; dependency or toolchain changes require renewed qualification.
Ordinary pool admission still rejects the incomplete scheduler lifetime profile. Component limits do not reserve simultaneous worker/coordinator storage.

Observed allocations check the source derivation and do not define its limits. Isolated finalizer timings do not establish transactions per hour or performance improvement. Broader workloads, nonempty-child full-size merges, sustained throughput, multiple GPUs and AMD/Metal qualification remain open.
